title: Anchor metrics relay and call-graph contextualization for noise-aware SLO paging
creator: Marin Alvarez
description: Problem: Our current SLO paging system triggers noisy on-call pages when upstream batch jobs or non-customer traffic spike metrics. Existing burn-rate rules consider single signals (error rate, latency P99) without preserving runtime call-graph context or metadata from the metrics/log relay. This leads to false positives and poor oncall signal-to-noise.
goal: Deliver a metrics-relay anchoring layer that preserves trace-derived call-graph tags and a lightweight contextualization pipeline that weights SLO signals by call-graph importance. Use this to compute a noise-aware burn-rate score used by paging policies and anomaly detectors, reducing false pages by >40% while preserving detection of real degradations.
success_metrics: Reduction in PAGER incidents attributed to noisy upstream jobs >= 40% compared to baseline
Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for true SLO violations does not increase more than 10%
Burn-rate alert precision increases by 25% in post-rollout evaluation
No measurable regression in e2e SLO detection latency (< 30s additional processing)
Landing in obs-2026.03 release and dashboards published
implementation_steps: Design: define anchored payload schema for metrics-relay that includes trace call-graph tag, service_role, and request_origin (internal|external)
Ingest: extend metrics-relay sidecar to attach call-graph tags for sampled traces and propagate via metrics envelope
Indexing: augment observability backend to store anchor tags alongside time series as low-cardinality dimensions
Contextualization: implement a scoring lambda that computes per-route weight factors (customer-facing routes > internal batch routes)
Burn-rate integration: modify burn-rate engine to multiply signal weights and compute a noise-aware burn_score used for paging thresholds
Pager policy: add routing rules that suppress pages for low-weighted signals and send aggregated watchlist notifications instead
Evaluation: run shadow mode for 72h comparing existing and weighted burn-rate decisions with synthetic and historical datasets
Rollout: staged rollout to 10% services -> 50% -> 100% with canary dashboards and automated rollback on metric regressions
acceptance_criteria: Anchored metrics payload documented in Confluence and schema validated by two services
Metrics-relay sidecar implemented and deployed to dev cluster with sampling opt-in flag
Backend index stores anchor tags without >2x write amplification
Noise-aware burn_score available in the alerting pipeline and used by a canary pager policy
Shadow evaluation data shows >=25% reduction in false positive pages before rollout
Runbook updated with new pager escalation and suppression semantics
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy metrics-relay sidecar with anchor opt-in to non-prod and 2 demo services. 2) Enable backend indexing and validate queries. 3) Run contextualizer in shadow mode for 72h across 20% traffic. 4) Enable noise-aware burn_score for paging policy on 10% of services and monitor. 5) Gradually increase to full rollout with revert on automated safety checks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Anchor tags increase cardinality and storage costs. Mitigation: restrict to low-cardinality tags and enforce sampling/backpressure
Risk: Legitimate customer-facing errors suppressed incorrectly. Mitigation: conservative initial weightings and canary with human-reviewed samples
Risk: Added processing latency. Mitigation: scoring pipeline must be sub-30s; use async enrichment and cache recent route weights
Risk: Instrumentation gaps across services. Mitigation: provide library helpers, codegen snippets, and a fall-through classification based on endpoint patterns
